shell.reason: The pushed Consumer route uses CatchRouteScaffold so route chrome, scroll-under behavior, and surface ownership remain canonical.

topBar.reason: The city-access application is a compact Settings spoke with canonical back navigation and a scroll-derived divider.

stateController.primary: LaunchAccessApplicationScreen resolves current-user and application provider waves; LaunchAccessController owns one typed draft and submit mutation.
stateController.notes: The route is available from normal Consumer Settings. Firestore remains authoritative for the current user's application, status locking, submission count, and server timestamps; the form never writes local JSON or a client-only launch gate.

designRefs.notes: Focused widget tests prove the form-shaped loading state and canonical CatchField host-interest control.
Controller tests prove draft editing, current-user submission, and route-lifecycle reset.
Repository tests prove creation, editable updates, locked-status rejection, and Firebase provider ownership.

states.source: Application stream failures render through CatchAsyncBoundary with an exact provider retry.
states.nextAction: Keep provider failures on the shared branded error surface.

states.source: Offline application reads use the shared offline recovery state and exact retry owner.
states.nextAction: Keep offline classification centralized in CatchAsyncBoundary.

states.source: Non-editable application statuses replace the form with an explicit review or approval result.
states.nextAction: Keep status labels and editability derived from LaunchAccessApplicationStatus.

states.source: LaunchAccessController.submitMutation validates the draft and delegates one current-user transaction to LaunchAccessRepository.
states.nextAction: Preserve transaction-owned status locking and duplicate-submit exclusion.

states.source: The editable form has deterministic text-scale and reduced-motion capture witnesses.
states.nextAction: Keep long labels and choice groups overflow-free as application options evolve.

composition.currentLayout: CatchRouteScaffold with one provider-aware route adapter and a scrollable CatchFieldLanes application form.
composition.targetLayout: The current layout is canonical: route ownership stays at the screen, while the form remains a reusable typed section driven by LaunchAccessController state.

sections.name: Launch access application form
sections.migration: Keep the form on shared CatchField and CatchChoiceInput.form primitives; do not reintroduce a client-only launch gate or local snapshot authority.
